scope: Second fixed-optimum practice wave plus broad empirical model-class denominator; interpretation audit remains incomplete.

new_direct_empirical_target.citation: Voje KL. 2020. Testing eco-evolutionary predictions of fossil data using a scaling exponent. Evolution.
new_direct_empirical_target.system: Yellowstone fossil diatom valve-diameter time series
new_direct_empirical_target.adequacy_caution: Present: the paper explicitly reports imperfect model adequacy and notes that the OU runs test is only barely passed.

direct_denominator_candidate.citation: Gearty W, McClain CR, Payne JL. 2018. Energetic tradeoffs control the size distribution of aquatic mammals. PNAS.
direct_denominator_candidate.system: fossil Sirenia, Pinnipedia, Odontoceti and Lutrinae time series
direct_denominator_candidate.note: The study fits fossil time-series OU models with the paleoTS joint parameterization, but the strongest mechanistic half-life language in the paper is intertwined with phylogenetic OU analyses. Count as a direct-likelihood denominator candidate only; fixed-time-series mechanistic numerator coding remains unresolved pending supplement-level source audit.

systematic_model_denominator.meaning: Broad model-class prevalence context only; not an interpretation-frequency estimate.

interpretation: The fixed-optimum theorem now targets at least three independent empirical systems with explicit attraction/selection or adaptation-speed interpretation, including one case with explicit model-adequacy caution. Separately, the PETS saved-object audit shows that fixed or moving OU is the minimum-AICc candidate for 125 of 630 successful broad empirical comparisons. This strengthens practice relevance without licensing a prevalence claim about causal overinterpretation.
hard_stops: do not count Gearty 2018 in the mechanistic numerator until the fossil time-series interpretation is source-coded separately from phylogenetic OU results
do not use 3 confirmed examples as a field prevalence fraction
do not conflate model inadequacy with causal nonidentifiability
do not treat an adequacy warning as equivalent to an F4 causal-nonuniqueness warning
